note: Final (passes 1-4 merged). publications.aap.org, acog.org, pubmed and medlineplus blocked WebFetch, so open mirrors (CDC, AAFP, Merck Manual, PMC, HealthyChildren) were used. Immunization status checked 2026-10-01: CDC's Jan 5 2026 memo cut routine childhood recommendations (rotavirus, influenza, hep A, hep B, meningococcal and COVID moved to shared decision-making; RSV moved to high-risk). A federal court stayed that memo and the reconstituted ACIP's votes on 2026-03-16, restoring the June 2024 schedule, and the government is appealing. AAP publishes its own 2026 schedule, which keeps routine recommendations for 18 diseases. The lesson's hedge is accurate as of this date.

questions.note: At 21 days this infant is in the AAP 2021 8-21 day group, where full workup and admission are still recommended.
USPSTF 2022 recommends screening ages 12-18 (grade B). The 'systems for follow-up' wording comes from the 2016 statement, but this is still the only defensible choice.

claims.claim: In the US, WHO growth standards are recommended from birth to 2 years and CDC charts from age 2.
claims.note: CDC: WHO standards from birth to 2 y. From 2 y, the CDC 2000 charts, or the 2022 extended BMI charts for very high BMI.

claims.claim: AAP (2020 clinical report) recommends standardized developmental screening at 9, 18 and 30 months and autism-specific screening at 18 and 24 months.
claims.note: The CDC page lists the AAP ages. The source is Lipkin & Macias, Pediatrics 2020;145(1).

claims.claim: By 3 years a child is understood by strangers about three-quarters of the time.
claims.note: CDC's 2022 wording is 'talks well enough for others to understand, most of the time'. The 2022 CDC/AAP checklists use the 75th percentile, so independent walking is listed at 18 months, not 12.

claims.claim: The Apgar score describes condition and response to resuscitation, does not decide whether to start resuscitation, and does not predict long-term outcome on its own.
claims.note: AAP/ACOG joint statement, 2015.

claims.claim: The AAP 2022 hyperbilirubinemia guideline uses hour-specific thresholds based on gestational age and neurotoxicity risk factors; jaundice in the first 24 h needs measurement.
claims.note: Published in Pediatrics in September 2022 and applies to infants of 35 weeks or more.

claims.claim: CCHD pulse-oximetry screening is done at 24 hours or later, and a failed screen leads to echocardiography (fail if below about 90 percent or a persistent hand-foot difference).
claims.note: CDC confirms the timing of 24 h or more and echocardiography after a failed screen. The page does not show numeric cutoffs. The AAP algorithm (2020, updated in a 2025 clinical report) fails below 90%, passes at 95% or more in both sites with a difference of 3% or less, and allows one repeat.

claims.claim: Maternal GBS screening at 36 to 37 weeks with intrapartum prophylaxis (AAP 2019 report).
claims.note: The window is 36 0/7 to 37 6/7 weeks. The 2019 AAP and ACOG documents replaced the CDC's 2010 guidance.

claims.claim: Early-onset sepsis presents in the first 72 hours, mainly GBS and E. coli.
claims.note: 72 hours is the common definition, and E. coli now rivals or exceeds GBS, especially in preterm infants. Some GBS definitions use 0-6 days.

claims.claim: Antenatal corticosteroids accelerate lung maturity and reduce RDS; RDS shows ground-glass lungs with air bronchograms.
claims.note: Merck: corticosteroids given at 24-34 weeks reduce RDS risk and severity.

claims.claim: About 4 percent of Down syndrome cases are Robertsonian translocations.
claims.note: CHOP gives 3-4%.

claims.claim: The AAP health supervision report for Down syndrome dates from 2022.
claims.note: Published May 2022 in Pediatrics (Bull et al.).

claims.claim: Fragile X is caused by changes in FMR1 and is the most common inherited cause of intellectual disability.
claims.note: CDC says 'one of the most common causes of inherited intellectual disability'. The page does not detail the CGG repeat or premutation disorders.

claims.claim: A sweat chloride of 60 mmol/L or more is diagnostic of cystic fibrosis.
claims.note: 2017 CFF consensus: 60 or more diagnostic, 30-59 intermediate, under 30 unlikely.

claims.claim: Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency is an X-linked urea cycle disorder.
claims.note: OTC is at Xp11.4 and is the most common urea cycle disorder.

claims.claim: SMA (SMN1 deletion) is now on many newborn screening panels because early gene-based therapy works best.
claims.note: Understated. SMA was added to the RUSP in 2018 and all 50 states have screened since February 2024.

claims.claim: Cytomegalovirus is the most common congenital infection and hearing loss is its main long-term morbidity.
claims.note: CDC: the most common infectious cause of birth defects in the US, about 1 in 200 newborns. Hearing loss is the most common long-term problem.

claims.claim: Folic acid supplementation before conception reduces neural tube defect risk.
claims.note: 400 mcg/day, or 4,000 mcg after a previous NTD pregnancy.

claims.claim: Ultrasound is the DDH imaging study before 4 to 6 months, then radiography, and the Pavlik harness treats young infants.
claims.note: AAP 2016 clinical report (Shaw & Segal). The PDF was read through a text extractor.

claims.claim: US schedule is under active revision and organisations differ, so consult the current schedule; core: HepB in infancy, DTaP/Hib/IPV/PCV/rotavirus from 2 months, influenza from 6 months, Tdap/HPV/MenACWY in adolescence.
claims.note: Current as of 2026-10-01. CDC's Jan 2026 memo moved hep B, rotavirus, influenza, hep A, meningococcal and COVID to shared decision-making. A court stayed it on 2026-03-16 and restored the June 2024 schedule, and the government has appealed. AAP's 2026 schedule (hep B birth dose, rotavirus at 2 months, influenza from 6 months) matches the lesson. The lesson says the CDC schedule is 'published jointly' with AAP/AAFP, which is historical: in 2026 AAP published a separate schedule.

claims.claim: The 1998 paper claiming an MMR-autism link was retracted.
claims.note: Retracted by The Lancet in February 2010.

claims.claim: Measles herd immunity requires roughly 95 percent coverage.
claims.note: Estimated at 93-95% two-dose coverage.

claims.claim: The AAP 2021 guideline gives a stepwise approach for well-appearing febrile infants 8 to 60 days using urinalysis, ANC, CRP and procalcitonin.
claims.note: The guideline sets three age bands: 8-21, 22-28 and 29-60 days.

claims.claim: All febrile infants 28 days or younger get blood, urine and CSF cultures, empirical IV antibiotics and admission.
claims.note: Too absolute under AAP 2021. Full workup and admission are mandatory only for 8-21 days. At 22-28 days, well-appearing infants with negative inflammatory markers and urinalysis can be managed without admission (LP based on markers). Ill-appearing infants and those under 8 days are outside the guideline.

claims.claim: Renal and bladder ultrasound is recommended after the first febrile UTI; VCUG for abnormal ultrasound or recurrence.
claims.note: AAP 2011 guideline for ages 2-24 months, reaffirmed in 2016.

claims.claim: AAP 2013 AOM guideline: diagnosis needs a bulging TM or new otorrhoea; observation is an option in selected older children with mild disease; amoxicillin is first-line.
claims.note: Observation applies to age 2 or older with non-severe illness. Amoxicillin is given at high dose, 80-90 mg/kg/day.

claims.claim: In children a negative rapid strep test is followed by throat culture (IDSA 2012); penicillin/amoxicillin treatment prevents rheumatic fever.
Measles: Koplik spots, rash spreading from the face downward, SSPE years later, vitamin A given.
claims.note: CDC confirms these. It lists pneumonia among the common complications but does not single it out as the most common cause of death.

claims.claim: The AAP 2014 bronchiolitis guideline advises supportive care and against routine bronchodilators, corticosteroids, antibiotics, radiographs and chest physiotherapy.
claims.note: Published in Pediatrics in November 2014. No newer AAP bronchiolitis guideline was found.

claims.claim: RSV prevention uses nirsevimab or clesrovimab for infants, or maternal RSV vaccination in late pregnancy.
claims.note: Clesrovimab (Enflonsia) was approved by the FDA in June 2025 and recommended by ACIP in June 2025 for infants under 8 months whose mothers were not vaccinated. Abrysvo is given at 32-36 weeks, September to January. Infants get either the maternal vaccine or an antibody, not both. CDC's Jan 2026 memo moved RSV to high-risk while still recommending it for infants of unvaccinated mothers; that memo is stayed. AAP recommends routine use.

claims.claim: NHLBI asthma guidance was updated in 2020 (after 2007) toward combined ICS-formoterol reliever approaches in some ages.
claims.note: SMART (single maintenance and reliever therapy) from age 4.

claims.claim: Pyloric stenosis presents at about 2-8 weeks, mostly in boys, with hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis; fluid correction comes before pyloromyotomy.
claims.note: Merck gives 3-6 weeks typical onset and a 5:1 male ratio.

claims.claim: Hirschsprung: failure to pass meconium within 48 hours, rectal suction biopsy confirms, associated with Down syndrome.
Intussusception is usually ileocolic at 6 months to 3 years; ultrasound shows a target sign; air or contrast enema reduces it.
claims.note: Merck: reduction succeeds in over 80%. Currant-jelly stool is a late sign.

claims.claim: Congenital heart disease affects about 1 percent of live births and is the commonest birth defect; VSD is the most common lesion.
Kawasaki diagnosis: fever for 5 or more days plus 4 of 5 features; IVIG within the first 10 days with aspirin reduces aneurysms (AHA 2017).
claims.note: The 1.5 cm node size was not stated on the opened page.

claims.claim: TGA: egg-on-a-string, PGE1 and balloon atrial septostomy before an arterial switch.
claims.note: The association with maternal diabetes was not shown on this page.

claims.claim: In DKA total body potassium is depleted despite normal/high serum K; cerebral oedema presents with headache, bradycardia, hypertension and altered consciousness (ISPAD 2022).
claims.note: The CPS statement cites ISPAD 2022. Treatment is 3% saline or mannitol.

claims.claim: Precocious puberty: before age 8 in girls and 9 in boys; delayed puberty: no breast development by 13 or no testicular enlargement by 14; boys more often have pathology needing imaging.
claims.note: AAFP 2025 also notes that race-based cutoffs are no longer valid.

claims.claim: CAH is most commonly 21-hydroxylase deficiency, confirmed by elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone and detected by newborn screening.
claims.note: About 95% of cases.

claims.claim: AAP 2011: after a simple febrile seizure, no routine imaging, EEG or labs; LP considered with meningeal signs, incomplete immunization, and in those under 12 months.
claims.note: The 2011 guideline removed age alone as an LP criterion. LP is an option at 6-12 months only when Hib or pneumococcal immunization is deficient or unknown, or after antibiotic pretreatment. 'Under 12 months' as a standalone criterion comes from the 1996 guideline. The rest of the claim is supported.

claims.claim: Childhood absence epilepsy: 3-Hz spike-and-wave, provoked by hyperventilation, ethosuximide first-line.
Infantile spasms: hypsarrhythmia, tuberous sclerosis a common cause, first-line ACTH or corticosteroids, vigabatrin especially in TSC.
claims.note: Merck gives a peak of 4-6 months; the lesson's 3-8 months is consistent.

claims.claim: Anaemia screening is recommended at about 12 months.
claims.note: AAP 2010 clinical report (Baker & Greer). USPSTF considers the evidence insufficient.

claims.claim: ALL is the most common childhood cancer, peaking at 2 to 5 years.
Neuroblastoma: opsoclonus-myoclonus, raised urinary catecholamine metabolites, MYCN amplification predicts poor prognosis.
TEN-4-FACESp flags torso, ear or neck bruising under 4 years and any bruising in an infant under 4 months.
claims.note: The rule says '4 months and younger' (validated as 4.99 months or younger), not 'under 4 months'. It also includes the frenulum, angle of the jaw, cheeks, eyelids, subconjunctivae and patterned bruising.

claims.claim: A skeletal survey is recommended for suspected physical abuse in children younger than 2 years.
claims.note: AAP and ACR.

claims.claim: Clinicians are mandated reporters in all US states; the threshold is reasonable suspicion; CAPTA conditions state systems; good-faith reporters have immunity.
claims.note: Child Welfare Information Gateway summary of state statutes, read through a PDF text extractor.

claims.claim: USPSTF (2022) recommends screening for major depressive disorder in adolescents 12 to 18.
claims.note: Grade B, October 2022. Evidence is insufficient for suicide-risk screening and for children 11 and under.

claims.claim: Cervical screening begins at 21 and is not needed earlier.
claims.note: USPSTF 2018 recommends against screening under 21 (grade D). The page says the topic is being updated.

claims.claim: Leading causes of teen death are accidents (mainly motor vehicle crashes), then suicide and homicide.
claims.note: In 2023 the order was unintentional injury, homicide, then suicide. Firearms have been the leading mechanism of adolescent injury death since 2017, ahead of motor vehicle crashes, so 'mainly motor vehicle crashes' is dated.

claims.claim: AAP 2019 ADHD guideline covers ages 4-18; parent training is first-line for preschoolers, with methylphenidate if behavioural treatment fails.
Enuresis is wetting during sleep after age 5; primary means never dry for 6 months; the alarm is most effective long-term, and desmopressin suits short-term needs.
M-CHAT-R/F autism screening is recommended at 18 and 24 months (AAP).
